AI answer sheet checking

# Handwritten copies, checked by AI in a teacher's red pen.
Upload a whole class's scanned answer sheets at once. Evalezy reads every student's name, marks each answer against one marking scheme, and hands back the student's own copy with ticks, crosses, notes and the total circled. You review and release.

Pause logos

The pile
After every exam, a teacher carries home a stack of copies and gives up evenings and weekends to check them.

The drift
Copy 5 and copy 95 are not marked the same way. Neither are two teachers checking the same paper.

The number
Under time pressure, students get a score and a few ticks, rarely the reason they lost marks.

What makes Evalezy different

## Not a score table. The copy itself, checked.
Most AI graders give you a number per question. Evalezy writes back onto the student's own pages, the way a teacher would, so students can see exactly where marks were won and lost.

How it works

## From question paper to released results in four steps.

Every step in detail

- 01 Upload the question paper
It is read into questions with their marks. Fix anything in a minute, no retyping.

- 02 Set the marking scheme
Accept the AI's draft for each question, edit it, or write your own with model answers.

- 03 Upload every copy at once
Up to 200 PDFs. Names and roll numbers are read from each sheet and matched to your students.

- 04 Review, then release
Marks fill in live. Change any mark, then release. Students get their checked copy by email.

Bulk upload & student matching

## Drop in 200 copies. Each one finds its student.
Scan the whole section into one folder and upload it. Evalezy reads the name, roll number and class written at the top of each copy and matches it to your students. When it is not sure, it asks you instead of guessing.

- Phone photos or scanner PDFs, one file per student, up to 60 MB each
- Reading names is free; you pay only for pages checked
- Copies with no name or two close matches wait for you to pick
- Or check the copies students uploaded themselves in one click
- A bell alert and an email when the batch is done

Consistent marking, teacher control

## One marking scheme for every student. The final word for every teacher.
Each question gets a scheme once, used for copy 1 and copy 200 alike. Then the marks land as a draft for you to review, change and release.

1. The AI drafts the scheme; you can change every line

AI draft Your scheme

- Names valid factors of climate (latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, relief, winds) 1.5
- Explains how each factor affects climate 1
- Uses a correct example 0.5

Built to be trusted with marks

## Careful where it matters.
We do not publish an accuracy percentage; it depends on handwriting, scans and your scheme. Here is what Evalezy does instead to keep marks right.

Answers found by content
Students answer out of order. Evalezy matches each answer to its question by what it says, not by the number written beside it.

Maths gets a second read
Equations and working are read from the page; lines it is unsure of go to a dedicated equation reader.

Never guesses an unreadable page
If most of a copy cannot be read, the check stops with a clear reason. No invented marks, and no charge.

Marks that add up
Criteria always sum to the question's marks, marks come in half steps, and every deduction gets one clear note.

Never guesses a student
No name, a weak match or two close names? The copy waits for you to pick. It is never filed under the wrong student.

Teachers have the last word
Marks are a draft until released. A teacher's edit is never overwritten, even if the copy is checked again.

- 1–8 minutes a copy, several at once. First results in about 10 minutes.
100 copies in about 2–3 hours. Upload in the evening, review in the morning.
Diagrams are judged by labels and explanation only; keep a teacher on those.

One copy, checked twice

## Building an edtech product? Put a red pen in it.
Grade handwritten copies and typed long answers from your own exam system. Create an exam, upload each candidate's PDF, and read question-wise marks, reasons, feedback and the checked copy. ## Questions teachers ask us
More in the full FAQ .

How accurate is it? +
We do not publish an accuracy percentage, because it depends on handwriting, scan quality, subject and how good the marking scheme is. What we do instead: every mark comes with the student's answer as read and the reason for the mark, low-confidence questions are flagged for review, unreadable copies are never guessed, and nothing reaches students until a teacher releases it. Try it on your own copies in a demo.

Can teachers change the AI's marks? +
Yes, any mark on any question. The review screen shows the student's answer as read, the AI's feedback and the criteria breakdown. A mark a teacher edits is never overwritten, even if the copy is checked again.

Do I need a scanner? +
No. Phone photos combined into a PDF work. The sample copy on this site is a phone photo of a spiral notebook. Pages are straightened, cleaned and contrast-boosted before reading.

How does it know which copy belongs to which student? +
It reads the name, roll number and class or section written at the top of the first page (or the second page's header) and matches it to the students in that assessment. If there is no name, the match is weak, or two students are close, it does not guess: the copy waits for you to pick the student or skip it.

What about diagrams, maps and graphs? +
Grading works from what is written. Diagrams are judged by their labels and the written explanation, not as drawings. For questions that are mostly a diagram, keep a teacher on the final mark.

How long does it take? +
Usually 1 to 8 minutes per copy, with several copies checked in parallel. The first results appear in about 10 minutes; 100 copies take roughly 2 to 3 hours. You get a bell alert and an email when a batch is done.

What is not charged? +
Failed checks, stopped checks and unreadable copies are free. Reading names and matching copies to students is free.

Is there an API? +
Yes. With the Evaluation API your own system creates an exam with its questions and rubrics, uploads each answer sheet as a PDF (or sends typed answers), and reads back question-wise marks, reasons, feedback and the checked copy. You poll for results (there are no webhooks yet), and marks stay drafts until you finalize them. We switch it on per institute: write to hello@evalezy.com or request access on the demo page. Full docs at docs.evalezy.com.

# How AI Answer Sheet Checking Works, Step by Step | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/how-it-works/

- Home
- / How it works
How it works

# How Evalezy checks a handwritten answer sheet.
Three steps for you, eight for the machine, and a review before anything reaches students. Here is every step, including the ones that keep it from guessing.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

Your part

## Set up once per paper

- 1. Create the assessment and upload the question paper
The paper is read into questions with their marks, sections and printed numbers. Edit anything that needs it.
More
- 2. Check the marking scheme
Each question gets criteria that add up to its marks. Accept the AI draft, edit it, or write your own and add model answers.
More
- 3. Upload the copies
Drop in up to 200 PDFs, one per student; or let students upload their own in an online test. Names and roll numbers are read and matched; anything uncertain waits for you.
More

Evalezy's part · 1–8 minutes a copy

## What happens to each copy

- 1 Read the page layout
Each page is straightened, cleaned and contrast-boosted, and the position of every written line is found. Printed-text OCR alone cannot read handwriting, so it is only used for where lines are, never for what they say.

- 2 Read the handwriting
A vision model reads every line as written, three pages at a time, row by row. It is told never to invent text; anything it cannot read is marked as unreliable.

- 3 Check the copy is readable
If most pages are too blurred or blank to read, the check stops here with a clear reason. No marks are guessed and nothing is charged.

- 4 Second read for maths
Up to four maths lines the reader was unsure of are sent to a dedicated equation reader and replaced with its reading.

- 5 Find each answer
On copies of four pages or more, Evalezy works out which pages hold which answer, by content, so answers written out of order are still found. If a question then looks unattempted, the whole copy is searched again before it gets zero.

- 6 Mark each question
Each answer is marked against its criteria, in half-mark steps, with the student's own words quoted. Low-confidence marks are re-asked. Marks appear on your screen question by question.

- 7 Make the marks add up
Marks are capped at the maximum, criteria scaled to match, and each question gets exactly one score and one clear note.

- 8 Write on the copy
Ticks, crosses, corrections, notes and marks are drawn onto the student's pages in a handwriting-style red pen, with the total circled on page one.

Several copies are checked at once. The first results usually appear within about 10 minutes of uploading, and 100 copies take roughly 2 to 3 hours. Copies up to 40 pages are read in full.

Your part again · as long as you like

## Review and release

- 4. You are notified
A bell alert and an email when the batch is done.

- 5. You review
Answer as read, marks, feedback and criteria per question. Change any mark; your edit is kept.

- 6. You release
Students get their checked copy by email. Until then they see "Results pending".

Teacher review in detail

# The student's own copy, checked the way a teacher would.
Evalezy does not stop at a score. It writes back onto the student's pages: a tick where marks were earned, a cross with the correct answer where they were not, a short note where an answer fell short, marks in the margin and the total circled on page one.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

Page two of a checked copy: ticks, a 0/1 with 'Wrong answer. Correct: Mohenjo-daro', 1.5/2 with a note on what the definition missed, and 2/2 with 'Good.'

## Anatomy of a checked page
Tap a number to see what each mark means.
Page one of the sample answer copy checked by Evalezy 1 2 3 4 5

- 1 The total, circled Marks are added up and the total is circled at the top right of page one, the way a teacher does. Here: 38 out of 80.
- 2 A tick on what earned marks Correct answers get a red tick on the line itself, drawn with a slightly uneven hand so it reads as pen, not stamp.
- 3 Marks per question, in the margin Every question gets its marks written beside it, in half-mark steps where the scheme allows.
- 4 A cross, with the correct answer Wrong answers get a cross and the correct answer beside it: "Wrong answer. Correct: latitude (distance from the equator)."
- 5 A note where marks were lost Incomplete answers get a short note explaining what was missing, so the student knows what to fix, not just that they lost a mark.

Half marks, with a reason

## Partial credit you can see.
Marks are given in half-mark steps against the question's criteria. When an answer earns part of the marks, Evalezy writes what was missing next to it, so “1.5/2” comes with a reason.

- One score per question, written in the margin
- One clear note per deduction, never a wall of text
- Short, kind praise where an answer is complete

Two answers on the copy: 1.5/2 with the note 'Q21: Methodology and purpose of Social Science not mentioned.' and 2/2 with 'Good.'

Long answers

## Notes on what a long answer missed.
On 3- and 5-mark answers, the note names the gap: a missing part, a missing example, a list where an explanation was asked for. It sits right under the answer, in the same red pen.
The note is written for the student, not the teacher: what to add next time.

A long answer marked 3.5/5 with the note: 'How to Produce' lacks production techniques; 'What' lacks detail on goods.

## The marks on every copy

- Tick on what earned marks
- Cross, with the correct answer beside it
- 1.5/2 Marks per question, in half-mark steps
- note A short note where marks were lost

Read the full 7-page sample

## Frequently asked questions
Why does the checked copy look handwritten? +
Because students and parents trust a copy that looks checked. Notes are drawn in a handwriting-style font with a slight wobble, ticks are drawn as uneven pen strokes, and the ink is a teacher's red. The same copy always re-renders identically.

Can teachers edit the checked copy? +
Teachers change marks and feedback on the review screen; marks they edit are kept and never overwritten by the AI. The marks students see are the marks the teacher released.

How do students get it? +
When a teacher releases results, each student receives the checked copy as a PDF by email. Results can also go out on WhatsApp through Automations if you have connected WhatsApp.

How big is the checked PDF? +
Page images are re-encoded so the checked PDF stays under 18 MB, small enough to email, even for a long phone-scanned copy.

## Evalezy never guesses a student.
A copy filed under the wrong name is worse than a copy not checked. So matching is strict, and anything uncertain comes to you.
What was read from the copy | Result |

Unique roll number on the sheet | Matched |
Name matches one student clearly | Matched |
Roll number shared by two students | You pick |
Two students with very similar names | You pick |
No name found, or a weak match | You pick |
A second copy for a student already matched | You pick |

Scanning tips
One PDF per student, pages in order. Phone scanner apps work well. Keep the whole page in frame and avoid deep shadows across the writing.

Limits
Up to 200 files per upload and 60 MB per file. Copies up to 40 pages are read in full.

Timing
Usually 1–8 minutes a copy, several at once. First results in about 10 minutes; 100 copies in roughly 2–3 hours.

## Frequently asked questions
What does the student need to write? +
Their name, and ideally roll number and class or section, at the top of the first page, the way they already do. Evalezy reads the top of page one first, then the whole first page, then the top of page two if needed.

What if a student wrote their name in Hindi? +
Names written in other scripts are read and transliterated so they can be matched against the names in your student list.

Does reading names cost anything? +
No. Reading and matching names is free. You pay only for the pages that are checked.

What happens to copies that don't match? +
They wait in the Bulk checks panel with the reason (no name found, two close matches, a duplicate). Pick the student from a scored list of suggestions, or skip the copy. Nothing is checked under a guessed name.

Can students upload their own copies instead? +
Yes. In an online test set to manual evaluation, students upload a PDF of their answer sheet. Check all submitted copies with one click, select a few and check those, or switch on auto-check so each copy is checked as soon as it is submitted. Already-checked copies are skipped unless you choose to re-check.

How will I know when it's done? +
The batch settles as completed or needing review, and you get a bell alert and, if you ticked the box, an email with the counts.

## Frequently asked questions
What format should the question paper be in? +
A PDF of the paper as you printed it. Typed papers work best; a clear scan of a printed paper also works.

Can I fix a question it read wrongly? +
Yes. Every question and mark can be edited before you check any copies.

We already uploaded copies to a test without questions. Can we still use AI checking? +
Yes. A test that only has an "upload your answer sheet" placeholder cannot be AI-checked, so the Submissions tab offers to read the attached question paper into questions and adopt them for that test.

Do I also need a marking scheme? +
Evalezy drafts one per question automatically the first time a copy is checked, so you can start without one. Most teachers review the draft or add model answers for the long questions first.

# AI Marking Scheme Generator, or Bring Your Own Rubric | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/marking-scheme/

- Home
- / AI marking scheme
AI marking scheme

# One marking scheme per question. The same for every student.
Consistency starts with the scheme. Evalezy drafts criteria for each question that add up exactly to its marks, you edit what you want, and that scheme is used for every copy in the assessment.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

Q30 · Explain the factors affecting climate.
3 marks · Section C

AI draft Your scheme

- Names valid factors of climate (latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, relief, winds) 1.5
- Explains how each factor affects climate 1
- Uses a correct example 0.5
Criteria add up to 3 / 3
Model answer (optional)
Latitude, altitude, pressure and wind system, distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief features…

Used for every student in this assessment

Why it matters

## Copy 1 and copy 200 are judged the same way.
When a person checks 200 copies, the standard drifts: generous early, strict late, or the other way round. When several teachers share a paper, each brings their own standard.
Evalezy fixes the scheme before the first copy is checked and uses it for every copy. That is the single biggest reason AI checking can be fairer than a tired human, and why we ask you to read the scheme first.

Copy 1 · Q30
Named weather elements, not climate factors

0.5 / 3
Copy 87 · Q30
Three factors, explained, no example

2.5 / 3
Copy 200 · Q30
Factors, effects and an example

3 / 3
Illustration: three different answers to the same question, all judged against the same three criteria.

Guidance, not formulas

## Criteria describe quality. The marks stay with the criterion.
Each criterion says what a good answer does: names the factors, explains the effect, gives an example. The marks live on the criterion, not inside the wording, so editing one never silently caps another.

- Marks awarded in half-mark steps
- Per-criterion marks shown on the review screen
- Edit a criterion and every later check uses the new version

## Frequently asked questions
How many criteria does a question get? +
One for objective questions (one-mark answers and anything with options). Three to five for subjective questions, each with its share of the marks.

What if the criteria marks don't add up? +
They always do: criterion marks are rescaled so they sum exactly to the question's maximum marks.

Can I use my board's marking scheme? +
Yes. Replace the AI draft with your own criteria per question, or set a fixed scheme for the whole assessment. Add a model answer per question if you have one; a stored model answer is used ahead of anything generated.

Does the AI look for exact wording? +
No. A model answer is a reference, not wording the student must match. Answers that say the right thing in different words still earn the marks.

When is the scheme created? +
Once per question, the first time a copy of that assessment is checked, and then reused. Two copies starting at the same moment still get one scheme, not two.

# The AI checks. The teacher decides.

## From check to release

- 01
Watch it fill in
Marks appear question by question while a copy is being checked. Stop a check at any time; a stopped check is not charged.

- 02
Get told when it's done
A bell alert and an email when a batch finishes, so nobody has to keep checking the screen.

- 03
Review and adjust
For each question: the student's answer as read, the marks, the feedback and the criteria. Change any mark and its feedback.

- 04
Students wait
Until release, students see "Results pending". Marks and the checked copy are held back on the server.

- 05
Release
Release one student, a selection or the whole assessment from the Submissions tab.

- 06
Students receive the copy
Each student is emailed their checked copy as a PDF. Add WhatsApp through Automations.

Built-in safety

## Marks students can trust.

- A total is only final when every question is graded; a partly checked copy never shows a misleading total
- A released result is not changed by a late AI callback
- Edited marks are labelled and recorded with who changed them and when
- Unreadable copies fail clearly instead of getting guessed marks

Stop
Halts within seconds. Not charged.

Edit
Marks clamped between 0 and the question's maximum.

Release
Email with the checked copy attached; WhatsApp via Automations.

## Frequently asked questions
What happens to my edits if the copy is checked again? +
They are kept. A question a teacher has edited is never overwritten by a later AI check.

Can students see anything before release? +
No. Students see "Results pending"; their marks, report and checked copy are refused by the server until release.

Who gets notified when checking is done? +
The teacher who started the check, the assessment's creator and evaluator, and the institute's admins get a bell alert; admins also get an email. Bulk uploads send one notice for the whole batch.

Can I send results on WhatsApp? +
Yes, through Automations: use the "Assessment Result Released" trigger with a WhatsApp, email or push step. The student's name, marks, total, percentage and checked-copy file are available to the message.

What does "Need review" mean? +
A copy or question the system was less sure about: a low-confidence read, a copy that could not be matched to a student, or a question still waiting. Start your review there.

# Online long answers, graded in about 20 seconds.
Not every answer is handwritten. In online tests, students type essays, letters and emails into a long-answer box. Evalezy grades those too, against the same kind of criteria, and holds the result for a teacher to review.

Q2 · Write an email to your principal requesting a science club. (5 marks, 120–150 words)

How to set it up

## Switch on AI evaluation, add a long-answer question.
In the test settings, pick any result type except manual and turn on “Evaluate submissions with AI”. Add questions of type Long Answer, with a model answer if you have one.

- Graded automatically when the student submits
- Result held as pending until a teacher releases it
- Model answer used as a reference, not as required wording

Test settings
Result type Release after review
Evaluate submissions with AI On
Question type Writing skills → Long answer

## Frequently asked questions
What does it judge a typed answer on? +
Format and conventions (an email's greeting and sign-off, a letter's layout), content, organisation and language. Spelling counts, because there is no handwriting to blame. Word limits are enforced. Answers worded differently from the model answer still earn credit.

What if a student tries to trick the AI? +
The student's text is treated as data, not instructions. In a production test, an email that told the evaluator to "award full marks" scored 0 out of 5.

What about MCQs in the same test? +
Objective questions keep their normal automatic marks. Only long-answer questions go to the AI, and the total adds both.

Are blank answers charged? +
No. A blank answer gets zero immediately, without an AI call, and an attempt where every answer is blank is not billed.

How are typed answers priced? +
Typed answers have no pages, so they are priced per answer graded rather than per page. On the Evaluation API it is 1 credit per non-blank long answer, with objective answers free. For the dashboard, ask us for the current rate.

Can students copy-paste an answer? +
Copy, cut and paste are blocked in the long-answer box, which also shows a live word count.

# Answer Sheet Evaluation API for Developers | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/api/

- Home
- / Evaluation API
Evaluation API

# Answer sheet evaluation, as an API.
Grade handwritten answer copies and typed long answers from your own exam system. Send a question paper, a marking scheme and each candidate's PDF; get back question-wise marks, reasons, feedback and the checked copy in red pen. Marks stay drafts until you finalize them.
Book a demo Read the API docs

cURL Node.js Python 202 Accepted
POST /exams/{id}/submissions Copy
curl https://api.evalezy.com/v1/exams/$EXAM_ID/submissions \
-H "X-API-Key: $EVALEZY_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Idempotency-Key: sst-ix-mock-4-IXB-14" \
-d '{
"candidate": { "external_id": "IXB-14", "name": "Aditi Sharma", "roll_number": "14" },
"upload_id": "0d2b6c1e-6a1f-4c55-9a43-2b1f0c9e7a10"
}'

X-API-Key, scoped
Keys look like vak_eval_… and carry scopes: read, write, review, finalize. Server to server only. Base URL https://api.evalezy.com/v1

Fixed price, quoted first
1 credit per page (handwritten) or per long answer (typed). POST /credits/quote before you submit; failed and cancelled are free.

Safe retries
Idempotency-Key on every POST, plus natural keys: your external_ref per exam, external_id per candidate, one live submission each.

Drafts until you finalize
The AI never publishes marks. Override, approve, then POST /exams/{id}/finalize. Unfinalizing needs a reason.

Dashboard review included
API exams show up in the Vacademy dashboard, tagged Source: API, so teachers can review without you building a screen.

Full reference and guides
Every endpoint with request, response and code, guides for term exams, typed tests and daily answer writing, and an OpenAPI document.

## The flow, in six calls
Ten-minute quickstart

- 1.

### Create an exam
Questions, max marks, answer keys for objective questions and a rubric or model answer for long answers. Opening it fixes the questions, marks and answer keys; rubrics and model answers stay editable.
In the docs
POST /exams Copy
curl https://api.evalezy.com/v1/exams \
-H "X-API-Key: $EVALEZY_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Idempotency-Key: sst-ix-mock-4" \
-d '{
"title": "Social Science · Half-Yearly Mock Test 4",
"mode": "handwritten",
"external_ref": "sst-ix-mock-4",
"class": "9",
"open": true,
"questions": [{
"label": "30",
"type": "long_answer",
"text": "Explain the factors affecting climate.",
"max_marks": 3,
"rubric": { "criteria": [
{ "name": "Names valid factors of climate", "marks": 1.5 },
{ "name": "Explains how each factor affects climate", "marks": 1 },
{ "name": "Uses a correct example", "marks": 0.5 }
]}
}]
}'

- 2.

### Upload the answer sheets
One PDF per candidate. Ask for presigned URLs (up to 100 per call), PUT each file, then read the upload back to confirm its page count.
In the docs
POST /uploads Copy
# 1. Ask for a presigned upload URL (1 to 100 PDFs per call, 50 MB each)
curl https://api.evalezy.com/v1/uploads \
-H "X-API-Key: $EVALEZY_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"filename": "IXB-14.pdf", "content_type": "application/pdf", "size_bytes": 8421337}'

# 2. PUT the PDF to the upload_url it returns (no API key on this call)
curl -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" --data-binary @IXB-14.pdf

- 3.

### Submit each copy
Name the candidate by your own id and pass the upload_id; typed tests send answers[] instead. You get 202 and a fixed-price quote straight away.
In the docs
POST /exams/{id}/submissions Copy
curl https://api.evalezy.com/v1/exams/$EXAM_ID/submissions \
-H "X-API-Key: $EVALEZY_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Idempotency-Key: sst-ix-mock-4-IXB-14" \
-d '{
"candidate": { "external_id": "IXB-14", "name": "Aditi Sharma", "roll_number": "14" },
"upload_id": "0d2b6c1e-6a1f-4c55-9a43-2b1f0c9e7a10"
}'

- 4.

### Follow grading
Poll one submission, or the feed of everything that changed since your last sync. Webhooks are on the roadmap; polling is the supported way today.
In the docs
GET /submissions?updated_since= Copy
# No webhooks yet: poll the feed and follow next_cursor until has_more is false
curl "https://api.evalezy.com/v1/submissions?updated_since=2026-10-02T10:00:00Z" \
-H "X-API-Key: $EVALEZY_API_KEY"

- 5.

### Read results and the checked copy
Question-wise marks, criteria with reasons, feedback, the answer as read, confidence and needs_review, plus the red-pen PDF.
In the docs
GET /submissions/{id}/result → 200 Copy
{
"submission_id": "5a7e2c90-1b4d-4e8f-a3c2-7d9e0f1a2b3c",
"status": "graded",
"needs_review": true,
"finalized": false,
"totals": { "awarded": 38, "max": 80, "percentage": 47.5 },
"questions": [
{
"label": "30",
"awarded": 0.5,
"max": 3,
"source": "ai",
"confidence": 0.88,
"needs_review": false,
"extracted_answer": "1. Temperature 2. Humidity 3. Precipitation 4. Atmospheric Pressure 5. Wind",
"feedback": "Only weather elements listed; no factors of climate explained.",
"criteria": [
{ "name": "Names valid factors of climate", "awarded": 0.5, "max": 1.5, "reason": "Lists weather elements, not factors." },
{ "name": "Explains how each factor affects climate", "awarded": 0, "max": 1, "reason": "No explanation." },
{ "name": "Uses a correct example", "awarded": 0, "max": 0.5, "reason": "No example." }
]
}
],
"checked_copy": { "available": true, "download_path": "/submissions/5a7e2c90-…/checked-copy" },
"credits_charged": 7
}

- 6.

### Review, then finalize
Override any mark (free) or approve it, in your app or in the Vacademy dashboard. Marks are drafts until you finalize.
In the docs
POST /exams/{id}/finalize Copy
curl -X POST https://api.evalezy.com/v1/exams/$EXAM_ID/finalize \
-H "X-API-Key: $EVALEZY_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"all_graded": true}'

Example values come from the real sample copy on this site (Class IX Social Science, 7 pages, 38/80).

## Key endpoints
Full API reference
Base URL https://api.evalezy.com/v1. These are the calls most integrations use; the reference lists all of them.
Method | Path | What it does |

POST | /exams | Create an exam with its questions, marks, answer keys and rubrics or model answers. Send open: true to accept submissions straight away. |
POST | /exams/{id}/open | Open a draft exam to accept copies. Rubrics must add up to max marks; questions, marks and answer keys are then fixed. |
PUT | /exams/{id}/questions/{qid}/rubric | Set one long-answer question's rubric and model answer. Without one, a rubric is generated on the first copy and reused. |
POST | /candidates | Create or update up to 2,000 candidates by your own external_id. Or skip it and send the candidate with the submission. |
POST | /uploads | Get presigned URLs for 1 to 100 PDFs (50 MB each), PUT each file, then read it back to check its page count. |
POST | /exams/{id}/submissions | Submit one candidate's copy (upload_id) or typed answers. Returns 202 with a fixed-price quote. |
GET | /submissions?updated_since=… | The feed of every submission that changed, across exams. Poll it to pick up results (no webhooks yet). |
GET | /submissions/{id}/result | Question-wise marks, criteria with reasons, feedback, the answer as read, confidence and needs_review. |
GET | /submissions/{id}/checked-copy | Download the checked copy: the student's PDF with ticks, crosses, notes and marks. |
PATCH | /submissions/{id}/questions/{qid} | A teacher's override: marks (0.5 steps) and feedback for one question. Overrides are free. |
POST | /exams/{id}/finalize | Publish draft marks as final, for chosen submissions or every graded one. Nothing is final until you call it. |
POST | /credits/quote | Quote the fixed price before you submit, and check your balance covers it. |

## Submission statuses

- queuedWaiting for a grading slot, with queue position and estimated ready time.
- processingGrading has started.
- readingThe handwriting is being read.
- gradingAnswers are being marked.
- gradedEvery question was graded. Marks are drafts until you finalize.
- partially_gradedAt least one question could not be graded; a teacher marks it.
- failedThe copy could not be graded, e.g. unreadable. Reason in error.code. Not charged.
- cancelledYou cancelled it. Not charged.

## Not in the API yet
Planned, without dates. The docs' roadmap says what to do today for each.

- Webhooks: poll the submission feed for now
- Phone photos: send one PDF per answer sheet
- Bulk scans split and matched by name: one PDF per candidate
- Exams from a question-paper PDF: send questions as JSON
- CSV results and Hindi or regional-language answers
API roadmap

Ready to build?
Read the docs, then ask us to switch the Evaluation API on for your institute. Tell us what you are building and your expected monthly volume.

API docs Request API access

## Frequently asked questions
How do I get an API key? +
The Evaluation API is switched on per institute. Write to hello@evalezy.com (or use the demo page) to get it enabled. An institute admin then creates keys in the Vacademy dashboard under Settings → Integrations → API keys, with only the scopes each system needs.

Is there a sandbox? +
No. Every key is live and every graded copy is billed. Try things with a small exam of one or two short copies; failed and cancelled copies cost nothing.

Are there webhooks? +
Not yet; they are on the roadmap. Today you poll GET /submissions?updated_since= with a single worker, which the docs walk through step by step.

What can I upload? +
PDFs only, one per answer sheet, up to 50 MB each. Copies up to 40 pages are graded normally; 41 to 80 pages are graded and flagged for review; longer ones are refused before any charge. Phone photos must be combined into a PDF first.

How is it priced? +
1 credit per page of a handwritten PDF, blank pages included, and 1 credit per non-blank typed long answer. Objective answers are free. The price is fixed and quoted before grading; failed and cancelled copies are not charged; re-evaluating is charged again.

Do teachers have to use my app to review? +
No. Exams you create through the API also appear in the institute's Vacademy dashboard, tagged Source: API, where teachers can review and change marks. Their changes show up in your API results.

Which languages are supported? +
English answers only for now. Copies in Hindi or another regional language fail with language_not_supported and are not charged.

## Pricing questions
How much does it cost? +
₹1 per page checked in India, $0.01 per page elsewhere. A 7-page copy costs ₹7. There is no subscription and no setup fee. Indian prices exclude GST.

What is not charged? +
Failed checks, stopped checks and unreadable copies are free. Reading names and matching copies to students is free.

Is a re-check charged? +
Yes. Re-checking a copy runs a fresh check and replaces the marks, so it is billed again. Teacher edits are free and are kept.

Is the API priced differently? +
Not for handwritten copies: the API charges 1 credit per page of the PDF, blank pages included, the same ₹1 or $0.01 a page as the dashboard. Typed tests on the API are priced per answer: 1 credit per non-blank long answer, and objective answers are free. The price is fixed and quoted before grading; failed and cancelled copies are not charged, and re-evaluating a copy is charged again. Details at docs.evalezy.com/platform/pricing.

Do you offer volume pricing? +
For large volumes (exam bodies, platforms) talk to us about capacity and pricing before your exam window.

# AI vs Teacher: One Answer Copy, Checked Twice | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/side-by-side/

- Home

AI vs teacher

# One answer copy. Checked twice.
A maths half-yearly mock test: 80 marks, 32 questions, 7 pages. A teacher checked it in green pen. Evalezy checked the same scan in red. Each caught mistakes the other missed, and that is exactly why Evalezy never releases marks without a teacher.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

Teacher · green pen
48/80
0 written notes

Evalezy · red pen
40/80
12 written notes

They disagreed on 10 of 32 questions:

- Slips Evalezy caught that the teacher ticked 2
- Answers Evalezy misread that the teacher got right 5
- Half-mark judgement calls 3

Page by page

## Drag across the page to compare.
Both copies are the same scan, so every difference you see is a difference in checking.
1 2 3 4 5 6 7

- Wipe Side by side

Page 1. Section A, one-mark answers. Both crossed Q3. They split on Q6: the student wrote −19/7, and Evalezy missed the minus sign.
Page 1, checked by the teacher in green penPage 1, checked by Evalezy in red pen

Teacher Evalezy
Teacher Evalezy Drag across the page or use the slider: teacher’s green pen on the left, Evalezy’s red pen on the right.

What Evalezy caught

## Two slips the teacher ticked.
Right final answers with wrong working: easy to tick past at copy 40. Evalezy checks every line against the scheme and says what went wrong.
Q30 · page 7 · student wrote A = 7, B = 6; check: 37 + 25 = 65
Evalezy caught it Teacher 3/3, check ticked Q30 as checked by the teacher: 3/3, check tickedEvalezy 2.5/3: “Check wrong: 37+25 = 62, not 65” Q30 as checked by Evalezy: 2.5/3: “Check wrong: 37+25 = 62, not 65”
The student’s own check says 37 + 25 = 65. It is 62. The teacher ticked it; Evalezy crossed it and wrote the right sum. The answer was right, so the slip cost half a mark.

Q28 · page 5 · student wrote 625t⁴/2, via × 25/2 t⁻⁸
Evalezy caught it Teacher 3/3 Q28 as checked by the teacher: 3/3Evalezy 2.5/3: exponent error and a 2/26 slip Q28 as checked by Evalezy: 2.5/3: exponent error and a 2/26 slip
Dividing by (2/25)t⁻⁸, the student wrote × 25/2 t⁻⁸ where it should be t⁸. The final answer is right; the working isn’t. The teacher gave full marks, Evalezy took half a mark and said why. (Evalezy also crossed one correct line, 5⁻³ = 1/125, by reading the 5 as a 6.)

What the teacher caught

## Five answers Evalezy misread.
A 7 read as a 1, a minus sign too small to see, a number the student had crossed out. The teacher read the handwriting correctly every time. These are the marks a teacher fixes in review before anything is released.
Q18 · page 2 · student wrote (c) ₹720
Teacher was right Teacher 1/1 Q18 as checked by the teacher: 1/1Evalezy 0/1: “Correct: (c) ₹720” Q18 as checked by Evalezy: 0/1: “Correct: (c) ₹720”
The student chose (c), the right option. Evalezy read ₹720 as ₹120 and marked it wrong, while its own note names (c) as correct.

Q6 · page 1 · student wrote (b) −19/7
Teacher was right Teacher 1/1 Q6 as checked by the teacher: 1/1Evalezy 0/1: “option b with minus sign” Q6 as checked by Evalezy: 0/1: “option b with minus sign”
The student chose (b) and did write the minus sign. Evalezy missed the small minus and marked a right answer wrong.

Q25 · page 4 · student wrote 7/30
Teacher was right Teacher 2/2 Q25 as checked by the teacher: 2/2Evalezy 1/2: “Common factor 7/5 missed” Q25 as checked by Evalezy: 1/2: “Common factor 7/5 missed”
The boxed answer is 7/30, which is right. Evalezy read the 7 as a 1, took a mark for a “missing” factor, and its note was cut off mid-sentence.

Q26 · page 4 · student wrote 350 km (corrected from 360)
Teacher was right Teacher 2/2 Q26 as checked by the teacher: 2/2Evalezy 0/2: “Correct answer: 350 km” Q26 as checked by Evalezy: 0/2: “Correct answer: 350 km”
The student struck out 360 and wrote 350 above it. Evalezy read the crossed-out number and gave 0/2, while naming 350 km as the right answer.

Q29 · page 6 · student wrote x = 5, y = 5 (both boxed)
Teacher was right Teacher 3/3 Q29 as checked by the teacher: 3/3Evalezy 2.5/3: “Final values not stated” Q29 as checked by Evalezy: 2.5/3: “Final values not stated”
Both values are boxed on the page. Evalezy took half a mark for not stating them.

Judgement calls

## Three half-mark differences.
Q27 · page 5 · student wrote 900 = 30²
Judgement call Teacher 3/3 Q27 as checked by the teacher: 3/3Evalezy 2.5/3: “Divisibility of 900 by 6, 9, 15 not verified” Q27 as checked by Evalezy: 2.5/3: “Divisibility of 900 by 6, 9, 15 not verified”
The answer is right. Evalezy wanted the student to show that 900 divides by 6, 9 and 15; the teacher didn’t. A strictness call.

Q32 · page 7 · student wrote Part (i) only
Judgement call Teacher 2/3 Q32 as checked by the teacher: 2/3Evalezy 1.5/3: “Part (ii) not attempted” Q32 as checked by Evalezy: 1.5/3: “Part (ii) not attempted”
Both took marks for the missing part (ii); they differ by half a mark. Evalezy’s note for this question was printed at the foot of page 4 by mistake.

Q22 · page 3 · student wrote 4a²/b²
Judgement call Teacher 2/2 Q22 as checked by the teacher: 2/2Evalezy 1.5/2: “Steps not shown clearly” Q22 as checked by Evalezy: 1.5/2: “Steps not shown clearly”
Evalezy took half a mark for unclear exponent steps; the teacher gave full marks. Settling who is right needs the question paper, which we don’t have.

## Every disagreement, in one table
Q | Student wrote | Teacher | Evalezy | Verdict |

Q6 | (b) −19/7 | 1/1 | 0/1: “option b with minus sign” | Teacher was right |
Q18 | (c) ₹720 | 1/1 | 0/1: “Correct: (c) ₹720” | Teacher was right |
Q22 | 4a²/b² | 2/2 | 1.5/2: “Steps not shown clearly” | Judgement call |
Q25 | 7/30 | 2/2 | 1/2: “Common factor 7/5 missed” | Teacher was right |
Q26 | 350 km (corrected from 360) | 2/2 | 0/2: “Correct answer: 350 km” | Teacher was right |
Q27 | 900 = 30² | 3/3 | 2.5/3: “Divisibility of 900 by 6, 9, 15 not verified” | Judgement call |
Q28 | 625t⁴/2, via × 25/2 t⁻⁸ | 3/3 | 2.5/3: exponent error and a 2/26 slip | Evalezy caught it |
Q29 | x = 5, y = 5 (both boxed) | 3/3 | 2.5/3: “Final values not stated” | Teacher was right |
Q30 | A = 7, B = 6; check: 37 + 25 = 65 | 3/3, check ticked | 2.5/3: “Check wrong: 37+25 = 62, not 65” | Evalezy caught it |
Q32 | Part (i) only | 2/3 | 1.5/3: “Part (ii) not attempted” | Judgement call |

Totals: teacher 48/80, Evalezy 40/80. Every other question was marked the same by both. Checked by hand against the student’s working on 2 October 2026; there was no question paper, so items that depend on it are judgement calls.

The point

## Neither checker got everything right. Together, they did.
Evalezy is more thorough about working, and writes a reason beside every lost mark. A teacher reads handwriting better. So Evalezy does the first check, a teacher reviews it, and nothing reaches students until the teacher releases.
How teacher review works Try it on your copies

- Both slips Evalezy caught stay caught: the teacher just confirms them
- All five misreads are visible on the review screen, with the answer as Evalezy read it, so they are quick to fix
- A teacher’s edit is never overwritten, even if the copy is checked again
- Students see nothing until the teacher presses Release

## Frequently asked questions
Is this a real teacher’s copy? +
Yes. A teacher checked this copy by hand. We ran the same scan through Evalezy and put the two side by side, unedited. We have left Evalezy’s mistakes in.

Why does Evalezy give 8 marks fewer? +
Two deductions are fair (Q30 and Q28: slips the teacher ticked). Five are Evalezy misreading handwriting (Q6, Q18, Q25, Q26, Q29): a 7 read as a 1, a small minus sign, a crossed-out number. The rest are half-mark judgement calls. A teacher reviewing Evalezy’s marks fixes those five in a few clicks.

So is AI checking better than a teacher? +
Not on its own, and we don’t claim it is. On this copy Evalezy was more thorough about working and wrote a reason for every lost mark; the teacher read handwriting better. Together they get it right, which is how Evalezy is built: AI first check, teacher review, then release.

Where does the teacher review happen? +
On the review screen: every answer as Evalezy read it, the marks, the reason and the criteria. A teacher changes any mark, and that edit is never overwritten. Students see nothing until the teacher releases.

## What to look for

- Tick on what earned marks
- Cross, with the correct answer beside it
- 1.5/2 Marks per question, in half-mark steps
- note A short note where marks were lost

- Phone photo, not a scanner. Shadows, a curved spiral notebook and ruled lines, all read.
- Half marks with reasons. 1.5/2, 0.5/3, 3.5/5: each with a note on what was missing.
- Mixed handwriting quality. Crossed-out words, insertions above the line and answers that run across pages.
- One slip, left in. Q17 on page 2 is right (“Egyptian Civilisation”) but was crossed. This is why a teacher reviews every copy before release.

# Evalezy FAQ: AI Answer Sheet Checking Questions | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/faq/

- Home
- / FAQ
FAQ

# Questions about AI answer sheet checking
How Evalezy marks, what it can and cannot read, how students are matched, what teachers control, what it costs and how the API works.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

## How it checks
What exactly does Evalezy do? +
It checks handwritten answer sheets. You upload scanned or photographed copies as PDFs; Evalezy reads the handwriting, finds each answer, marks it against a marking scheme for that question, and returns marks per question plus the student's own copy checked in red pen: ticks, crosses, short notes, marks in the margin and the total circled on page one.

How does it decide the marks? +
Every question gets a marking scheme: a few criteria whose marks add up exactly to the question's maximum. Evalezy can draft the scheme for you, or you can write your own and add a model answer. The scheme is created once per question and reused for every student, so all copies are judged the same way. Marks are given in half-mark steps.

How accurate is it? +
We do not publish an accuracy percentage, because it depends on handwriting, scan quality, subject and how good the marking scheme is. What we do instead: every mark comes with the student's answer as read and the reason for the mark, low-confidence questions are flagged for review, unreadable copies are never guessed, and nothing reaches students until a teacher releases it. Try it on your own copies in a demo.

Can students answer questions out of order? +
Yes. Answers are matched to questions by their content, not by the number the student wrote. On longer copies Evalezy first works out which pages hold which answer; if a question then looks unattempted, it re-checks the whole copy before giving zero.

Does it handle maths? +
Yes for written working and equations. Pages are read by a vision model, and maths lines it is unsure of get a second read by a dedicated equation reader.

What about diagrams, maps and graphs? +
Grading works from what is written. Diagrams are judged by their labels and the written explanation, not as drawings. For questions that are mostly a diagram, keep a teacher on the final mark.

Which languages does it support? +
Evalezy is built and tested on English answer sheets. Students' names written in other scripts are read and transliterated for matching. For Hindi-medium or other-language answers, send us sample copies and we will tell you honestly how it does.

Can it check typed answers from an online test? +
Yes. Long-answer questions typed in an online test (essays, letters, emails) are graded on format, content, organisation and language, with word limits. A typed answer takes about 20 seconds.

## Uploading copies
Do I need a scanner? +
No. Phone photos combined into a PDF work. The sample copy on this site is a phone photo of a spiral notebook. Pages are straightened, cleaned and contrast-boosted before reading.

How many copies can I upload at once? +
Up to 200 PDFs per upload, one file per student, up to 60 MB each. Copies up to 40 pages are read in full.

How does it know which copy belongs to which student? +
It reads the name, roll number and class or section written at the top of the first page (or the second page's header) and matches it to the students in that assessment. If there is no name, the match is weak, or two students are close, it does not guess: the copy waits for you to pick the student or skip it.

What if a copy is unreadable? +
If most pages are too blurred, dark or blank to read, the check fails with a clear message and you are not charged. Re-scan and upload it again.

Can students upload their own answer sheets? +
Yes. In an online test set to manual evaluation, students upload their answer sheet as a PDF. You can check every submitted copy with one click, or switch on auto-check so each copy is checked as soon as it is submitted.

How long does it take? +
Usually 1 to 8 minutes per copy, with several copies checked in parallel. The first results appear in about 10 minutes; 100 copies take roughly 2 to 3 hours. You get a bell alert and an email when a batch is done.

## Teachers, students and results
Can teachers change the AI's marks? +
Yes, any mark on any question. The review screen shows the student's answer as read, the AI's feedback and the criteria breakdown. A mark a teacher edits is never overwritten, even if the copy is checked again.

When do students see their results? +
Only after a teacher presses Release Result. Until then students see "Results pending" and the marks are hidden on the server, not just in the app.

How do students get the checked copy? +
On release each student is emailed their checked copy as a PDF. If you have connected WhatsApp in Automations, you can send results there too.

Can I stop a check that is running? +
Yes. Stop it from the progress screen; it halts within seconds and a stopped check is not charged.

## Pricing
How much does it cost? +
₹1 per page checked in India, $0.01 per page elsewhere. A 7-page copy costs ₹7. There is no subscription and no setup fee. Indian prices exclude GST.

What is not charged? +
Failed checks, stopped checks and unreadable copies are free. Reading names and matching copies to students is free.

Is a re-check charged? +
Yes. Re-checking a copy runs a fresh check and replaces the marks, so it is billed again. Teacher edits are free and are kept.

Is the API priced differently? +
Not for handwritten copies: the API charges 1 credit per page of the PDF, blank pages included, the same ₹1 or $0.01 a page as the dashboard. Typed tests on the API are priced per answer: 1 credit per non-blank long answer, and objective answers are free. The price is fixed and quoted before grading; failed and cancelled copies are not charged, and re-evaluating a copy is charged again. Details at docs.evalezy.com/platform/pricing.

Do you offer volume pricing? +
For large volumes (exam bodies, platforms) talk to us about capacity and pricing before your exam window.

## API and data
Is there an API? +
Yes. With the Evaluation API your own system creates an exam with its questions and rubrics, uploads each answer sheet as a PDF (or sends typed answers), and reads back question-wise marks, reasons, feedback and the checked copy. You poll for results (there are no webhooks yet), and marks stay drafts until you finalize them. We switch it on per institute: write to hello@evalezy.com or request access on the demo page. Full docs at docs.evalezy.com.

Who can see the answer sheets? +
Copies and marks live inside your institute's account. Students see their own results only after release. See the data and privacy page for details.

Who is behind Evalezy? +
Evalezy is built by the team behind Vacademy (Vidyayatan Technologies), a learning and assessment platform used by schools, online academies and training institutes across 5 countries. Evalezy is the AI checking engine of that platform, offered on its own.

# Data, Privacy and Control in AI Copy Checking | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/security/

- Home
- / Data & privacy
Data & privacy

# Your students' answer sheets, handled with care.
Answer sheets carry names, roll numbers and children's handwriting. Here is how Evalezy treats them, what stays in your control, and what we do not claim.
Book a demo

## Who sees what, and when

- Answer sheets, marks and checked copies live inside your institute's account.
- Students see only their own result, and only after a teacher releases it. Before release the server refuses their marks, report and checked copy, not just the app.
- Copies uploaded by teachers and copies uploaded by students are both held as pending until release.

## The AI never has the last word

- Every AI mark is a draft. A teacher reviews, edits and releases.
- A mark a teacher edits is never overwritten by a later AI check.
- A released result is not changed by a late AI update.
- A copy is never matched to a student by guesswork; uncertain matches wait for a person.

## When something goes wrong

- Unreadable copies fail with a clear reason instead of getting invented marks.
- If the checked PDF cannot be produced, the marks still arrive and can be reviewed.
- Failed, stopped and unreadable checks are not charged.
- Typed answers are treated as data, not instructions: an answer telling the AI to award full marks scored 0/5 in testing.

## How the checking is done

- Pages are processed by Evalezy's pipeline and by AI model and equation-reading providers it uses to read handwriting and mark answers.
- Each step only receives what it needs: page images for reading, answer text and criteria for marking.
- Usage is billed once per check, recorded against your institute.

## What we do not claim
Evalezy does not hold SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification today, does not offer on-premise deployment, and does not publish an accuracy percentage. If your procurement needs any of these, tell us early and we will tell you plainly where we stand. Evalezy is operated by Vidyayatan Technologies LLP under the Vacademy privacy policy .

# About Evalezy | Evalezy
URL: https://evalezy.com/about/

- Home
- / About
About

# We built the red pen we wished teachers had.
Evalezy comes from the team behind Vacademy, a learning and assessment platform used by schools, online academies and training institutes across 5 countries. Online tests were already easy to check. Handwritten copies were not: they still went home in a teacher's bag every weekend.
Book a demo

## Why the copy, not the score
Most automated grading stops at a number. But students do not learn from a number; they learn from seeing their own page marked: which line earned the tick, where the cross is, what the right answer was. Teachers know this, which is why they still check by hand. So we set out to return the copy itself, checked the way a careful teacher would check it.

## Why the teacher stays in charge
Marks matter to children and parents. An AI that publishes marks on its own is a liability. In Evalezy every mark is a draft, every deduction comes with a reason, unreadable copies are never guessed, and nothing reaches a student until a teacher releases it.

## Why ₹1 a page
Pricing should be something a school can work out on the back of an exam paper. Pages are what teachers count, so that is what we charge for, and nothing when a check fails.

## The name
Evalezy is evaluation, made easy. The logo is the loop a teacher draws around the total at the top of a copy, with a tick inside.

Evalezy
A Vacademy product · Vidyayatan Technologies LLP

## The problem today
Copies pile up after every exam
A teacher with four sections can carry 150+ copies home after one paper. Checking eats evenings and weekends, and results go out late.

Marking drifts across checkers
The same answer can get 2 marks from one teacher and 3 from another, or from the same teacher at copy 5 and copy 95.

Feedback stops at a number
Under time pressure, students get a score and a few ticks. They rarely see why they lost marks on a long answer.

## How it fits your workflow

- 1. Set the paper once
Upload the question paper; it is read into questions with marks. Accept the AI-drafted marking scheme or type your own.

- 2. Scan and upload the whole section
Phone photos or scanner PDFs, one file per student, up to 200 at a time. Names and roll numbers are read from the top of each copy and matched to the section.

- 3. Review on your own time
Marks fill in question by question. Open any copy, read the extracted answer and feedback, change a mark if you disagree.

- 4. Release when you are ready
Students see nothing until you press Release Result. Each student gets the checked copy as a PDF by email.

## What changes

- Every copy marked against the same scheme, from the first to the last
- A note on every answer that lost marks, in red pen on the copy itself
- Teachers stay the final word: edited marks are never overwritten
- Unreadable scans are flagged for a re-scan, not guessed and not charged

Worked example
four sections of 40, an 8-page half-yearly copy
160 copies × 8 pages × ₹1
₹1,280
$12.80 outside India · excl. GST · failed copies free

## Frequently asked questions
Does it work for CBSE, ICSE and state-board papers? +
Yes. Evalezy marks against the questions and marking scheme you give it, so the board does not matter. Upload your paper, check the drafted scheme against your board's marking guidelines, and edit any criterion before you run the check.

Our teachers check in notebooks, not answer booklets. Will phone photos work? +
Yes. The sample copy on this site is a phone photo of a spiral notebook. Pages are straightened and cleaned before reading. Very dark, blurred or cut-off photos fail with a clear message and are not charged, so you can re-scan them.

Can students see marks before the teacher checks them? +
No. AI marks are a draft. Students see "Results pending" until a teacher presses Release Result, and that rule is enforced on the server, not just hidden in the app.

What does it cost a school? +
₹1 per page checked. A section of 40 students writing an 8-page copy costs ₹320 for that paper. Failed and unreadable copies are free.

Checking caps how often you can test

## Frequently asked questions
Can we use our own model answers? +

Mentor time is the bottleneck

# Handwritten answer checking, as an API.
Your learners write on paper; your product lives online. Create the exam through the API, upload each answer sheet as a PDF (or send typed answers), and get back question-wise marks, reasons, feedback and the checked copy in red pen. Marks stay drafts until you finalize them.

## The problem today
OCR alone fails on handwriting
Printed-text OCR cannot read student handwriting, and a grader fed garbage text invents answers.

A score is not a product
Learners want to see their own page marked up, not a JSON blob turned into a table.

Building it in-house is a project
Page reading, answer location, rubrics, consistency, annotation, retries and a review screen for teachers are each a project of their own.

## How it fits your workflow

- 1. Create the exam
POST /exams with the questions as JSON: max marks, answer keys for objective questions, and a rubric or model answer for each long answer.

- 2. Upload each copy
One PDF per candidate, up to 50 MB, through presigned upload URLs (1 to 100 files per call). Typed tests send the answers as text instead.

- 3. Submit and follow
Submit each copy against your own candidate id. You get 202 and a fixed-price quote at once; poll the submission, or the updated_since feed for many.

- 4. Read, review, finalize
Question-wise marks with reasons, feedback, confidence, needs_review and the checked copy PDF. Teachers review in your app or the Vacademy dashboard; then you finalize.

## What changes

- Question-wise marks, criteria with reasons, feedback and confidence in JSON
- The student's own copy checked in red pen, as a PDF to show learners
- A needs_review flag on the answers a teacher should look at
- Teacher review without building a screen: API exams appear in the Vacademy dashboard
- ₹1 / $0.01 per handwritten page, quoted before grading; failed and cancelled copies are free

Worked example
20,000 answer sheets a month, 5 pages each
20,000 copies × 5 pages × ₹1
₹1,00,000

## Frequently asked questions
How do I get API keys? +
We switch the Evaluation API on for your institute: write to hello@evalezy.com or request access on the demo page with your expected monthly volume. An institute admin then creates keys in the Vacademy dashboard (Settings → Integrations → API keys), each with only the scopes it needs. There is no sandbox: every key is live and every graded copy is billed.

Is it synchronous? +
No. A handwritten copy usually takes a few minutes, so grading is asynchronous: the submit call returns 202 straight away with the submission id, its place in the queue, an estimated ready time and the fixed price. Poll GET /submissions/{id}, or the GET /submissions?updated_since= feed when many copies are in flight. Webhooks are not available yet.

What do I get back? +
The status and totals, and for each question: marks awarded out of the maximum, each rubric criterion with its marks and reason, feedback, the answer as read, a confidence score and a needs_review flag. For handwritten copies, GET /submissions/{id}/checked-copy returns the red-pen PDF. Marks are drafts until you call finalize.

What can I send? +
Handwritten copies as PDFs only, one per candidate, up to 50 MB; phone photos must be combined into a PDF first, and the API does not yet split a bundled scan or match copies by name. Copies up to 40 pages are graded normally; 41 to 80 pages are graded and flagged for review. Typed tests send each answer as plain text. Questions go in as JSON, not as a question-paper PDF. English answers only for now.

How is the API priced? +
1 credit per page of a handwritten PDF, blank pages included, and 1 credit per non-blank typed long answer; objective answers are free. At the standard rate a handwritten page costs ₹1 in India (excluding GST) or $0.01 elsewhere, the same as in the dashboard. The price is fixed and quoted before grading. Failed and cancelled copies are not charged; re-evaluating a copy is charged again. Details at docs.evalezy.com/platform/pricing.

# AI Copy Checking vs Manual Checking: An Honest Comparison | Evalezy

Compare

# Evalezy vs checking copies by hand
Teachers are the best judges of an answer. They are also tired by copy 80. Here is what changes when AI does the first check and the teacher does the final one.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

| Evalezy | Checking by hand |

Who decides the final mark | The teacher. AI marks are a draft until released | The teacher |
Time for 100 copies | About 2–3 hours of machine time, then a review | About 10 hours at 6 minutes a copy |
Consistency across copies | One scheme per question, applied to every copy | Drifts with fatigue and between checkers |
Feedback on the copy | A tick, cross or note on every answer, with the correct answer where it was wrong | Depends on the teacher's time |
Half marks | 0.5-mark steps against criteria | Yes |
Diagrams and drawings | Judged by labels and written explanation only | Fully judged |
Cost | ₹1 per page checked | Teacher time, or ₹/copy to outside checkers |
Unreadable handwriting | Flagged for review, never guessed, not charged | Teacher deciphers it |

## Choose checking by hand when

- The paper is mostly diagrams, maps or drawings
- It is a small class and the teacher has the time
- The answers are in a language Evalezy has not been tested on yet

## Choose Evalezy when

- Copies arrive in the hundreds after every test
- Several teachers or centres mark the same paper
- Students need written feedback, not just a score
- You want to test more often without adding checking load

## It is not either-or
Evalezy is designed to keep the teacher in charge. The AI does the reading and the first marking; the teacher reviews, edits any mark and decides when results go out. A teacher's edit is never overwritten by a later AI run.

## Where the time goes
By hand, most of the time goes into reading every line of every copy. With Evalezy, the reading is done for you: the teacher sees each answer as read, the marks, the reasons and the criteria, and spends their time on the answers where judgement matters.

## A real test: one copy, both ways
We ran a maths copy that a teacher had already checked through Evalezy. Evalezy caught two slips the teacher had ticked; the teacher read five answers correctly that Evalezy misread. Each caught what the other missed, which is why Evalezy's marks always wait for a teacher's review. Every page and every disagreement is on the AI vs teacher page.

## What students notice
A checked copy from Evalezy looks like a teacher checked it: red ticks, crosses with the correct answer, a note where marks were lost, marks per question and the total circled on page one. Students get more written feedback than a rushed manual check usually allows.

What most AI graders returnQ | Score | Remark |

Q4 | 0 / 1 | Incorrect |
Q5 | 0 / 1 | Incorrect |
Q6 | 0 / 1 | Incorrect |
Q21 | 1.5 / 2 | Partially correct |
Q30 | 0.5 / 3 | Partially correct |

A number per question. The student never sees where on the page they went wrong.
What Evalezy returns the copy itself Three answers marked wrong in red pen, each with the correct answer written beside it: latitude, lowest, Indus, and 0/1 in the marginA 3-mark answer listing weather elements, marked 0.5/3 with the note: Only weather elements listed; no factors of climate explained

Other comparisons
Evalezy vs on-screen marking (OSM) Evalezy vs ChatGPT

## Frequently asked questions
Will teachers trust AI marks? +
They do not have to. Every mark is a draft that a teacher can change, and the reasons are written next to each answer, so checking the AI's work is quick. Most teachers start by reviewing every copy, then focus on the ones flagged for review.

Is AI checking fair to students? +
It applies the same criteria to every copy, which removes the drift that comes with fatigue and multiple checkers. Fairness still needs a good marking scheme, which is why you can edit every criterion before you run the check.

# Evalezy vs on-screen marking (OSM)
On-screen marking moved checking from paper to a screen. Evaluators still read and mark every answer. Evalezy reads and marks first, so evaluators review instead.
Book a demo See a real checked copy

| Evalezy | Typical on-screen marking |

Who reads the answers first | AI, against a rubric per question | A human evaluator, on screen |
Evaluator effort per script | Review the AI's marks and reasons; change any mark | Read and mark every answer |
Consistency | Same criteria applied to every script | Depends on each evaluator, plus moderation |
Output for students | The script itself, annotated in red pen | Usually marks only |
Student matching | Names and roll numbers read from the script and matched automatically | Usually barcodes or manual entry |
Pricing | ₹1 per page | Varies; often licences or per-script fees, plus evaluator time |

## Choose typical on-screen marking when

- You need a mature, fully human evaluation workflow with barcoded booklets and evaluator panels
- Your regulations require every mark to be entered by a human evaluator

## Choose Evalezy when

- You want evaluators to review rather than read everything from scratch
- You want students to receive an annotated copy, not just marks
- You run frequent internal tests where an OSM setup is too heavy

## The difference in one line
OSM is a better desk for a human checker. Evalezy is a first checker. They can work together: Evalezy's marks, reasons and annotated copy give a human evaluator a head start, and the human's edits are kept.

## Setup
Evalezy does not need barcoded booklets. Students write on any paper; copies are scanned or photographed and the name and roll number are read from the top of the first page.

Can Evalezy work with our existing evaluation process? +
Usually yes. Teams use Evalezy for the first evaluation and keep their own reviewers for the final mark. If your scripts already run through your own system, the Evaluation API takes each one as a PDF and returns marks per question with reasons, as drafts your reviewers finalize.

## Choose a general chatbot when

- You want a quick second opinion on one answer
- You are drafting a model answer or a marking scheme to edit

- You are checking a class, a batch or an exam
- You want students to receive their own copy checked
- Marks must be consistent, add up and be reviewable

## Why one rubric matters
If each copy is checked in a fresh conversation, the standard can move from copy to copy. Evalezy creates the marking scheme once per question and uses it for every student, so the 1st and the 140th copy are judged the same way.

## Why the copy matters
Students learn from seeing their own page marked: which line earned the tick, where the cross is, what the correct answer was. Evalezy writes that back onto the copy in a handwriting-style red pen, with the total circled on page one.

# UPSC Mains Answer Writing Evaluation at Scale (and Where AI Helps) | Evalezy
